What Is Architectural Powder Coating?

Architectural powder coating is a finishing process in which dry, electrostatically charged powder is sprayed onto prepared building metalwork and cured in an oven. It forms a hard, even shell that protects the steel and aluminum parts used on and around buildings.

Unlike liquid paint, powder has no solvent carrier. The charged particles cling to the metal, then melt and cross-link in the oven, typically at 180 to 200 °C. That heat-driven reaction forms a continuous film that resists chipping, scratching and fading better than most sprayed paint, which is why powder coated railings and powder coated fences hold up well to weather.

The term architectural coatings covers finishes for building elements. This page focuses on exterior metal coating for railings, fences, gates and frames. Machinery and equipment belong to our [industrial powder coating](/services/industrial-powder-coating) page, and vehicle parts have their own pages.

Why choose powder over paint for building metal? Architectural powder coating applies in a controlled booth, cures without a solvent carrier and gives a thicker, more uniform finish than most brush or spray paint. It also reaches welds, joints and tube ends evenly, which is hard to do by hand on site. For most projects, professional architectural powder coating is the simpler route to a finish that lasts.
How Does Our Architectural Powder Coating Process Work?

Our architectural powder coating process follows six stages: inspection, stripping or blasting, pretreatment, masking, powder application and oven curing. Each stage protects the metal, and every part is checked before it leaves our Milton shop.

items: Inspection (on arrival). We check each railing, frame or fence section for rust, weld spatter, old coatings and damage. Please remove glass, gaskets, plastic parts and any hardware that heat could harm. Clear notes on the colour and finish you want help us quote accurately.
Stripping and blasting. Old paint, powder or rust is removed so the new finish bonds to bare metal. Heavy rust or mill scale may call for our [sandblasting services](/services/sandblasting) first.

Pretreatment. Washing, degreasing and rinsing remove oil, dirt and weld residue. Our [powder coating surface preparation](/services/surface-preparation) step is where an outdoor finish is won or lost.
Masking. Threaded holes, mounting faces and contact points are masked or plugged, so parts still fit and install cleanly on site.

Powder application. We spray your chosen colour electrostatically, reaching joints, tube ends and edges evenly. Clean, controlled application is the heart of architectural powder coating, and it is why we keep this step separate from preparation.
Oven curing. Each part cures at oven temperature, cools, and is inspected for coverage and smoothness before packing for pickup or delivery.

blocks.text: Timing matters. Typical shop orders follow our standard 48-hour turnaround, and we receive parts Monday to Friday, 7 AM to 5 PM. Long railing runs, heavy rust, several colours or large batches can need more time, so we confirm the schedule when we quote. We pack finished parts carefully for pickup or delivery to your site.
Which Parts Suit Architectural Powder Coating?

Most steel and aluminum building components suit architectural powder coating, including railings, fences, gates and frames, provided they fit our oven and handle curing heat. Send photos and dimensions, and we will confirm suitability before work starts.

items: Railings and stairs. Stair railing powder coating, balcony railing powder coating and handrail powder coating protect welded joints and tube ends, where weather attacks first. Aluminum railing powder coating suits lighter systems.

Fences and gates. Fence powder coating and gate powder coating suit steel and aluminum sections. Aluminum fence powder coating keeps lightweight panels uniform, while steel fence finishing seals the metal against rust.

Frames and canopies. Window frame powder coating, door frame powder coating and steel canopy powder coating give a clean, consistent look across a building. Aluminum window frames need careful masking at glazing edges.
Other metalwork. Ornamental ironwork and storefront metal finishing also suit architectural powder coating, and we handle other architectural metalwork on request.

blocks.text: To prepare for drop-off, label each section, remove loose dirt and take clear photos of any damage. Good photos let us quote architectural powder coating accurately and spot issues early. Larger assemblies can exceed oven limits, so check our [capabilities page](/capabilities) for size and weight limits before you order. Long runs can often be split into sections that fit, then joined on site.
What Finishes Does Architectural Powder Coating Offer?

Architectural powder coating offers gloss, satin, matte, textured and metallic finishes, with colours matched to a RAL code or a physical sample. We help you pick a finish that suits the building design and its exposure to sun and weather.

items: Popular looks. A matte architectural finish suits modern buildings, while textured powder coating hides minor surface marks on busy railings and gates.

Metallic and custom. A metallic architectural finish adds depth to feature elements. Custom architectural powder coating lets you match brand or building palettes, and our [custom powder coating colours](/services/custom-colors-finishes) page shows the wider range.
Matching. RAL colour matching helps you align new parts with existing metalwork. Send a sample or colour code, and we will recommend the closest powder, including custom architectural colours.
Exterior grade. Exterior-grade powder coating is chosen for weather exposure, so tell us where the part will be installed.

blocks.text: Not sure which finish fits? Send photos and tell us where the metalwork will be installed. A short chat before coating prevents surprises and keeps your architectural powder coating project on schedule. For weathered railings, our [restoration and recoating](/services/restoration-recoating) service handles stripping and railing recoating.
How Do We Check Architectural Powder Coating Quality?

We inspect every part before and after coating for even coverage, a smooth film, clean masked areas and a complete cure. Koojo is certified through the Absolute Bureau of Certification, and test reports are available on request.

Preparation drives results. Coating over clean, bare metal gives a corrosion-resistant architectural finish, because the cured film seals the surface against moisture. A reliable weather-resistant finish depends on that same bond, so we never rush stripping or washing.

Outdoor metal also faces sun. A UV-resistant finish and fade-resistant powder coating depend on choosing the right powder for the exposure. If your project calls for AAMA 2604 powder coating or an AAMA 2605 finish, tell us the specification at quote stage so we can confirm which powder and process suit it. Together, these steps create a durable outdoor metal finish.

Consistent architectural powder coating also means the next batch matches the last, because we keep records that support repeat orders. To keep finished metalwork looking sharp, wash it with mild soap and a soft brush, and avoid harsh abrasive cleaners. Our shop team reviews each batch against your order before packing. See our [certification page](/certification) to learn how we document our work.

Who Uses Our Architectural Powder Coating?

Contractors, railing installers, builders, property managers, municipalities and fabrication shops send us building metalwork most often. They want architectural powder coating that is dependable, fast and consistent from the first part to the last.

Crews from [contractors and construction](/industries/contractors-construction) often need steel and aluminum parts finished on a schedule, while [municipal and institutional](/industries/municipal-institutional) clients bring park, school and church metalwork. Commercial building metalwork and larger repeat jobs fit the full range of [powder coating services](/services) at our Milton shop. Reliable architectural powder coating also keeps maintenance simple for property managers. Whatever you build or maintain, we treat each part as a finished product and plan the coating around how it will be used.
Architectural Powder Coating FAQs

Short answer: yes, most steel and aluminum building metalwork can be coated, and typical shop orders return in 48 hours. These answers cover outdoor use, specifications, timing, recoating and preparation before you book.

blocks.q: Can architectural powder coating be used outdoors?
blocks.a: Yes. We select an exterior-grade powder for parts that face sun, rain and road salt. Tell us where the metalwork will be installed, and we will recommend a suitable powder.

blocks.q: Do you work to AAMA specifications?
blocks.a: If your drawings call for AAMA 2604 or 2605, send the specification with your quote request. We confirm which powder and process suit it before any work starts.

blocks.q: How long does architectural powder coating take?
blocks.a: Typical shop orders follow our 48-hour turnaround. Long railing runs, heavy rust, several colours or large batches are scheduled when we quote.
Yes. We strip the old coating, treat rust and prepare the bare metal before recoating. Heavily corroded sections may need repair by a fabricator first.

blocks.q: Can you match my building colour?
blocks.a: Yes. Send a RAL code or a physical sample, and we will recommend the closest powder. Slight variation can occur between powder batches and original finishes.

blocks.q: What should I remove before architectural powder coating?
blocks.a: Remove glass, gaskets, plastic parts and hardware that heat could damage. Label each section so we can return parts in the order you need for installation.
